title: Volume of Cubes and Cuboids
seo_title: Volume – JSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the volume of cubes and cuboids; find a missing length; change between cm³, m³ and litres. (summary of the NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 maths worksheets on volume: cubes and cuboids, the formula V = l × b × h, missing lengths, capacity in litres and tank problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Volume of a cuboid = length × breadth × height. Volume of a cube = l³.
  • Volume = area of base × height.
  • 1 cm³ = 1 ml, 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre, 1 m³ = 1,000 litres.

Examples

Example

Tank 2 m × 1.5 m × 1.2 m

3.6 m³

Answer: 3,600 litres

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the lengthsMultiply them.
Mixed unitsUse one unit.
Writing cm² for volumeVolume is in cm³.

items.q: The shaded base of this prism has area B. What is the volume of the prism?

items.q: A box is filled with cubes that have 12-centimetre edges. Each layer has 20 cubes, and there are 3 layers. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: Cubes: 20 × 3 = 60. Each cube is 18 cm³, so V = 60 × 18 = 7 12 cm³. (B × h works too: B = 20 × 14 cm², h = 3 × 12 cm.)

items.q: A prism has a base that is 3 12 cm long and 1 12 cm wide. It is 2 cm tall. Use B × h to find its volume.
items.e: B = 3 12 × 1 12 = 5 14 cm². V = B × h = 5 14 × 2 = 214 × 2 = 424 = 10 12 cm³.

items.q: How many litres of water can this tank hold?
A tank is 60 cm long, 45 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many litres of water can it hold?
A tank is 80 cm long, 50 cm wide and 45 cm high. How many litres of water can it hold?
The water in the tank is 20 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 40 × 30 × 20 = 24,000 cm³ = 24 litres (÷ 1,000).

items.q: The water in the tank is 35 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 60 × 40 × 35 = 84,000 cm³ = 84 litres (÷ 1,000).

items.q: The water in the tank is 28 cm deep. How many litres of water are in the tank?
items.e: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank: 50 × 25 × 28 = 35,000 cm³ = 35 litres (÷ 1,000).

items.q: 30 litres of water is poured into an empty tank. The tank is 40 cm long, 25 cm wide and 45 cm high. What is the depth of the water?
items.e: 30 litres = 30,000 cm³ (1 litre = 1,000 cm³). Depth = volume ÷ area of base = 30,000 ÷ (40 × 25) = 30,000 ÷ 1,000 = 30 cm.

items.q: 24 litres of water is poured into this empty tank. What is the depth of the water?
items.e: 24 litres = 24,000 cm³ (1 litre = 1,000 cm³). Depth = volume ÷ area of base = 24,000 ÷ (50 × 30) = 24,000 ÷ 1,500 = 16 cm.

items.q: 36 litres of water is poured into an empty tank. The tank is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. What is the depth of the water?
items.e: 36 litres = 36,000 cm³ (1 litre = 1,000 cm³). Depth = volume ÷ area of base = 36,000 ÷ (60 × 40) = 36,000 ÷ 2,400 = 15 cm.

items.q: A tank has a base 50 cm by 40 cm. 12 litres of water is poured into it. By how much does the water level rise?
Ada fills Tank A, 40 cm by 30 cm by 25 cm, to the brim with water. She then pours all the water into an empty Tank B with a base 50 cm by 40 cm. What is the depth of the water in Tank B?
items.e: Water in A = 40 × 30 × 25 = 30,000 cm³. Depth in B = 30,000 ÷ (50 × 40) = 30,000 ÷ 2,000 = 15 cm. The water is the same; only the base changes.

items.q: Mrs Musa's tank is 35 full. It has 36 litres of water in it. How many more litres of water are needed to fill the tank?
items.e: 3 units = 36 litres, so 1 unit = 12 litres. The empty part is 2 units = 2 × 12 = 24 litres. (The full tank is 5 units = 60 litres.)

items.q: A tank is 25 full of water. After 18 litres of water is added, it is 45 full. What is the capacity of the tank?
items.e: The 18 litres fills 45 − 25 = 25 of the tank. 2 units = 18 litres, so 1 unit = 9 litres. Capacity = 5 units = 5 × 9 = 45 litres.

items.q: Container A has 3 times as much water as Container B. Together they hold 48 litres. Kayode pours water from A into B until they have the same amount. How many litres does he pour?
items.e: 4 units = 48 litres, so 1 unit = 12 litres. A has 36 litres and B has 12 litres. Each needs 48 ÷ 2 = 24 litres, so pour 36 − 24 = 12 litres (1 unit).

items.q: An empty tank is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 50 cm high. A tap fills it at 8 litres per minute. How long does it take to fill the tank?
items.e: Capacity = 60 × 40 × 50 = 120,000 cm³ = 120 litres. Time = 120 ÷ 8 = 15 min.

items.q: A tank 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 45 cm high has water 15 cm deep. Water flows in from a tap at 6 litres per minute. How long will it take to fill the tank to the brim?
items.e: The empty part is 45 − 15 = 30 cm high: 50 × 40 × 30 = 60,000 cm³ = 60 litres. Time = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 min. (15 min would fill the whole tank, 90 litres.)

items.q: Aminat packs 3-cm cubes into a box 12 cm long, 9 cm wide and 6 cm high. How many cubes fit in the box?
items.e: Along the length: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Breadth: 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Height: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Cubes = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24. Or: the box is 648 cm³ and one cube is 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cm³, so 648 ÷ 27 = 24. (648 ÷ 3 = 216 divides by the edge, not the volume of a cube.)

items.q: A tank has a base 30 cm by 20 cm and contains some water. Kunle puts a stone into it. The stone sinks and the water level rises by 2 cm. Find the volume of the stone.
items.e: The stone pushes up a layer of water 30 cm by 20 cm by 2 cm. Volume of stone = 30 × 20 × 2 = 1,200 cm³.

items.q: Tank A has a base 40 cm by 25 cm and water 30 cm deep. Tank B has a base 50 cm by 30 cm and is empty. Water is poured from A into B until the water in both tanks is the same depth. What is this depth?
items.e: Water = 40 × 25 × 30 = 30,000 cm³. The two bases together are 1,000 + 1,500 = 2,500 cm². Depth = 30,000 ÷ 2,500 = 12 cm. (15 cm is half of 30, but the bases are not the same size.)

items.q: Abdullahi has a block of clay 20 cm by 12 cm by 8 cm. He cuts it into cubes with 4-cm edges. How many cubes does he make?
items.e: Clay = 20 × 12 × 8 = 1,920 cm³. One cube = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cm³. 1,920 ÷ 64 = 30 cubes. Check: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, 12 ÷ 4 = 3, 8 ÷ 4 = 2, and 5 × 3 × 2 = 30. (1,920 ÷ 4 = 480 uses the edge, not the volume of a cube.)
